text:
Maya: FYI customer reports Dedicated pool 'novus-prod' is taking ~60-120s to add replicas during spikes, causing 429s and timeouts. They say it used to be ~15s yesterday.

Maya: Posting logs they attached below, asking for quick mitigation and root cause triage.

Leo: I confirmed the account was not on a billing hold. Billing checked, nothing flagged.

Sam: Can we get pod events / kubelet logs from the new nodes? My first guess is imagepull/auth errors or init containers blocking.

Maya: Attaching minimal repro they ran: a simple ramp test to hit 120 rps for 30s which triggers autoscale. They ran curl against /generate.

Maya: They included this kube event excerpt:
```
Normal Pulling  Container image "registry.redwood.internal/runner:prod-202603"
Warning Failed   Failed to pull image "registry.redwood.internal/runner:prod-202603": rpc error: code = Unknown desc = failed to resolve credentials: token expired (401)
Warning BackOff  Back-off pulling image "registry.redwood.internal/runner:prod-202603"
Warning Failed   Error: ErrImagePull
```

Anika: That aligns with a token rotation hitting the internal registry. If many pods spin up at once they all race for fresh creds and the registry returns intermittent 401s. Kubernetes then backs off exponentially and that stretches pod readiness. Autoscaler sees pods not Ready and keeps scaling more slowly.

Ryan: Also seeing spikes of imagepull backoff correlated with our auth-rotation Lambda running every 5m. Ops-bot shows rotation at 11:17:02 and a small surge of pulls starting at 11:17:05.

ops-bot: [auth-rotation] service-token-refreshed for registry.redwood.internal at 2026-03-10T11:17:02Z

Sam: Ok. Two orthogonal factors: (1) registry 401s -> container creation delays; (2) autoscaler backoff logic treats create failures as progress vs capacity signal and stops aggressive adds. Both combine to cause apparent scale-up lag.

Jess: Short-term mitigation ideas: 
- Increase minReplicas for novus-prod from 2 -> 6 (fastest).
- Enable burst capacity for this tenant if allowed.
- Customer can push a warm image to a local node pool (pre-warmed) or we can pre-pull image on nodes.

Maya: Customer asked for one-click workaround. Can we do a manual bump now?

Jess: I can apply a temporary policy bump. Patching HPA/minreplica now.

ops-bot: [patch] scaling target novus-prod: minReplicas 2 -> 6 by Jess at 2026-03-10T11:21:37Z

Maya: After bump customer reports reduced errors within 90s, but still some 429s during first minute.

Sam: For a medium-term fix we should: (A) stagger credential refreshes across nodes to avoid synchronized 401 storm; (B) pre-warm image pulls on new nodes as part of provisioning; (C) change autoscaler heuristic to consider imagepull backoff as a recoverable transient rather than terminal.

Anika: Implementation note: we already have staggered refresh feature flag but it's not enabled for internal registry creds. I can flip the flag and roll a small change to apply to the agent that handles token refresh. That should reduce simultaneous auth failures.

Ryan: Also we can lower the kubelet/imagePull backoff ceiling for Dedicated pools to shorten retry delays (e.g., cap at 20s for first 3 attempts) — but need careful testing.

Sam: Quick repro steps for eng-runtime if you want to reproduce locally:
```bash
# simulate token expiry during scaleup
for i in {1..30}; do 
  kubectl run pulltest-$i --image=registry.redwood.internal/runner:prod-202603 --restart=Never -- sleep 300 &
done
# then rotate token in auth service and watch events
kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -n 40
```

Sam: Logs to collect: kube events, node-provisioning timeline, registry auth logs (token request timestamps), and autoscaler decisions. If you paste the events I can parse heuristics.

Maya: Customer provided full events; pasting a trimmed timeline:
```
11:16:58 scale request from reports -> target replicas 8
11:17:02 auth rotation triggered
11:17:05 20 pods started image pull
11:17:05-11:17:25 many 401s from registry
11:17:30 kube backoff -> pod restarts delayed 30s -> 60s -> 120s
11:18:45 first pod Ready
11:19:10 rps still high -> some 429s logged until 11:20:30
```

Jess: Helpful. That sequence is the cause: rotation collided with scale.

Maya: Customer wants ETA for permanent fix and asks for root cause doc for the support ticket.

Sam: Proposed short-term runbook for support ticket: 
1) If customer sees surge-slow scale and registry 401s, bump minReplicas temporarily or enable warm pool.
2) Verify auth-rotation schedule; if rotation aligns with customer surge windows, schedule rotation to a quieter window or enable staggered refresh.
3) Provide logs of imagepull 401s + events to eng-runtime for deeper fix.

Anika: I'll enable the staggered-refresh flag for internal registry creds on a canary host group today and monitor. If stable we'll roll to Dedicated fleets next week.

Ryan: I'll prototype reducing kubelet image pull backoff parameters in a staging cluster and run the rip-test. If results are good we can land the change.

Jess: Longer-term we should add an autoscaler signal: 'imagepull_pending' which triggers preemptive replica adds while backoffs happening. I'll open a ticket.

Maya: Thanks everyone. I'll update customer with the workaround (minReplicas bump) + ETA: canary flag flip today, infra testing next 48-72h.

Leo: I'll reach out to the customer owner and confirm they accept the temporary cost increase.

Maya: Closing loop here after sync with customer. Will re-open if new evidence. :thumbsup:
